apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: WorkflowTemplate
metadata:
  name: needle-ci
  namespace: argo-workflows
  labels:
    app: needle-ci
spec:
  # Backstop against a run that hangs before its pod ever starts (unbound
  # PVC, unschedulable, missing secret). Per-step activeDeadlineSeconds does
  # not cover that case: on 2026-08-07 five needle-ci runs sat Running for
  # 8h against a 3600s step limit. ttlStrategy only reaps COMPLETED runs, so
  # without a workflow-level cap they are never terminated and never GCd.
  # Basis: sum of per-step deadlines x attempts = 25500s, +50% headroom.
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 38400
  entrypoint: pipeline
  serviceAccountName: argo-workflow

  # Retain the pod when the workflow FAILS; clean up when it succeeds.
  #
  # The cluster default is OnPodCompletion, which deletes the pod the instant it
  # exits — a failed run leaves nothing but "exit code 101" and `kubectl logs`
  # returns NotFound. On 2026-08-05 that turned a one-line diagnosis into a full
  # local reproduction of a 1,711-test suite.
  #
  # OnWorkflowSuccess is the one that keeps failures around.
  podGC:
    strategy: OnWorkflowSuccess

  # Retain failed runs long enough to actually read them.
  ttlStrategy:
    secondsAfterSuccess: 3600      # 1h
    secondsAfterFailure: 172800    # 48h — survives overnight and a weekend day

  # Limit concurrent runs to prevent flooding the cluster.
  # Without this, repeated pushes during a workflow run create N concurrent
  # workflows (needle-ci had 4 in flight on 2026-08-07), all competing for
  # the same limited capacity and deadlocking on storage provisioning.
  synchronization:
    semaphore:
      configMapSemaphore:
        key: needle-ci
        namespace: argo-workflows

  volumeClaimTemplates:
    - metadata:
        name: workspace
      spec:
        accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
        # storageClassName MUST be explicit. Omitting it inherits the cluster
        # default, which on this Rackspace Spot cluster is `ssd` — banned by the
        # standing storage rule, and its Cinder backend rejects anything outside
        # 5-20Gi outright:
        #   ProvisioningFailed: failed to provision volume with StorageClass
        #   "ssd": Invalid input received: 'size' parameter must be between 5
        #   and 20
        # With the old `storage: 2Gi` and no class, every needle-ci run failed
        # to provision and its verify pod sat Pending forever (5 stuck at once,
        # oldest 100min, on 2026-08-07).
        storageClassName: sata
        resources:
          requests:
            # 2Gi could not hold this workspace regardless of the floor: the
            # verify step clones NEEDLE and runs a full Rust debug build plus a
            # 1,711-test suite, so target/ alone outgrows it. 10Gi matches the
            # proven `sata` sizes on this cluster and keeps concurrent runs
            # (routinely 5+) from flooding a small cluster. Cinder volumes
            # cannot be expanded in place, so this is a template edit if it ever
            # proves tight.
            storage: 10Gi

  # `check-version` writes its should-release decision to /output and reads it
  # back as an output parameter within the same pod, so a per-pod emptyDir is
  # sufficient — it must NOT share the workspace PVC, whose contents the release
  # step consumes as a clean git clone. The mount has existed since needle-ci was
  # split into verify/release stages, but the volume was never declared; the gap
  # stayed invisible because `verify` failed first on every run and
  # `check-version` was never reached.
  volumes:
    - name: output
      emptyDir: {}

  templates:
    # Main pipeline: verify always runs, release only when version changes
    - name: pipeline
      steps:
        - - name: verify
            template: verify
        - - name: check-version
            template: check-version-change
        - - name: release
            template: release
            when: "{{steps.check-version.outputs.parameters.should-release}} == true"

    # Verify stage: fast fail with fmt, clippy, check, then tests
    - name: verify
      activeDeadlineSeconds: 3600
      container:
        image: ronaldraygun/needle-ci-builder:0.1.5-with-deps
        command: [bash, -c]
        args:
          - |
            set -ex

            # Defensive: /workspace is a volumeClaimTemplate PVC, not a fresh
            # emptyDir. A pod reschedule/retry on this cluster's bursty
            # autoscaler can re-run this step against a PVC that already has
            # a partial clone from a prior attempt, and `git clone` refuses
            # to write into a non-empty directory. Clear it first so the
            # step is idempotent regardless of why it's re-running.
            rm -rf /workspace/* /workspace/.[!.]* 2>/dev/null || true

            git clone --depth 1 --branch main \
              "https://git.ardenone.com/jedarden/NEEDLE.git" \
              /workspace
            cd /workspace

            # First cargo/rustc call in the repo — rustup installs the toolchain
            rustc --version

            # Fast-fail checks: fmt, clippy, check
            cargo fmt -- --check
            cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
            cargo check

            # Run all unit tests and the sanitization latency assertion test.
            # Do NOT export SANITIZE_THRESHOLD_MS=10 here — 10ms is the test's
            # documented *release-build* target and is unreachable in debug
            # builds (observed CI median: ~170-580ms). Leave it unset so the
            # test uses its own build-mode-aware default (1500ms in debug builds,
            # 10ms in release builds).
            cargo test --lib
            cargo test --test sanitize_latency_assertion

            echo "Verify passed"
        env:
          - name: GIT_CONFIG_COUNT
            value: "1"

# NEEDLE Codex Guide

This file is the primary operating guide for Codex in this repository, both in
interactive sessions and when Codex runs headlessly as a NEEDLE worker. Inspect
the current repository state and the relevant source before relying on older
examples or planning documents.

## Project Overview

NEEDLE (Navigates Every Enqueued Deliverable, Logs Effort) is a Rust worker
binary. It selects and claims work through the repository's configured bead
backend, dispatches a coding agent, records telemetry, and routes every outcome
through an explicit state machine.

The primary backend is bead-rs (`bead`); bead-forge (`bf`) remains supported
for explicitly bound legacy workspaces. Check `.needle.yaml` and the `.beads/`
layout before running either CLI. Do not infer the backend from which binaries
happen to be installed, and never use one backend's repair or import command on
the other backend's database. `br` is retired and must not be introduced in
source, prompts, scripts, tests, or documentation.

## Working Safely

- Inspect `git status --short` before editing. Preserve unrelated user and
  worker changes in a dirty worktree.
- Multiple NEEDLE workers may share the same repository. Re-check files before
  modifying them and avoid broad rewrites that can overwrite concurrent work.
- **Do not create per-worker git worktrees to isolate concurrent workers** —
  a shared checkout is the intended model, not a bug to route around.
  Worktrees add disk and build-cache duplication without addressing the
  actual failure mode, which happens at the bead level: the same bead getting
  claimed and worked twice (confirmed 2026-08-09, commitgraph `cg-l0v0kc` —
  two byte-identical commits at the same second from two concurrent workers).
  The supported backends provide atomic claim operations, so avoid this by
  decomposing and dependency-ordering beads so the same unit of work is never
  independently claimable twice — see the target repo's own `AGENTS.md` for
  repo-specific guidance.
- Do not use destructive Git operations (`reset --hard`, forced checkout,
  forced push) to resolve unrelated changes.
- Forgejo (`git.ardenone.com`) is the authoritative remote. GitHub is a mirror.
  Push only to the configured `origin`, and never use `--force` or
  `--force-with-lease`.
- Keep commands suitable for unattended execution: avoid prompts, pagers, and
  commands that require an interactive terminal.
- Treat `docs/plan/plan.md` as architecture and design history. Verify current
  behavior in source and against the installed CLI before depending on old
  command examples.

## Rust Compatibility

The declared MSRV is Rust 1.75 (`Cargo.toml`). Do not add language features or
dependencies that require a newer compiler without intentionally updating the
MSRV and associated toolchain and CI configuration.

## Code Conventions

- Prefer `Result` and `?` for fallible operations. Do not hide operational
  failures with `unwrap()` or `expect()`. Reserve those calls for tests or a
  clearly documented invariant/unrecoverable initialization condition.
- Fallible public operations should return `Result`; infallible constructors,
  accessors, and pure transformations may return ordinary values.
- Match state and outcome enums exhaustively. Avoid catch-all `_` arms where a
  new variant should force an explicit decision.
- Emit telemetry for every state transition and terminal outcome.
- Preserve error context at process, filesystem, database, and parsing
  boundaries.
- Unit tests belong in `#[cfg(test)]` modules near their implementation.
- Integration and end-to-end tests belong under `tests/`.
- Use `#[tokio::test]` for asynchronous tests; do not introduce
  `tokio_test::block_on`.
- Prefer testing public behavior over implementation details.

## Critical Test Isolation

Any test that spawns the compiled `needle` binary as a real subprocess (for
example, `Command::new(CARGO_BIN_EXE_needle)`) must isolate both `HOME` and the
Explore strand's scan root.

Explore is enabled by default and otherwise scans under the real home
directory. An unisolated test can discover and mutate production bead stores.
This previously created hundreds of phantom beads across real repositories.

At minimum, give the subprocess a temporary home:

```rust
cmd.env("HOME", temp_dir.path());
```

Prefer also configuring `workspace_root` to a temporary fixture directory, or
disable Explore when the behavior under test does not require it. Never point a
test worker at `/home/coding` or another directory containing real projects.

## Verification

- Run `cargo fmt --check` for Rust changes.
- Run targeted tests for the modules or behavior changed.
- Run `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` when practical. Existing
  unrelated warnings must be reported distinctly rather than silently fixed as
  part of an unrelated task.
- On this host, the `cargo` wrapper may offload a clean repository to iad-ci and
  use a resource-limited local fallback for a dirty repository. Do not assume a
  command ran remotely; report what actually ran and its result.
- The authoritative full verification is the `needle-ci` workflow on iad-ci
  after a push to `main`. Do not claim full-suite success from targeted tests.
- If required CI fails, record the failure on the bead, fix it, and do not close
  the bead as successfully completed.

## Bead Workflow

Each bead supplies its own deliverables and acceptance criteria. Complete and
verify the requested repository work before closing it.

This repository is bead-rs-backed. Use:

```bash
bead close BEAD_ID --reason "Summary of what was done"
```

The close flag is `--reason`, not `--body`. When no code change is appropriate,
record the reason with a bead comment or another supported public `bead`
operation rather than creating an empty commit.

SQLite (`.beads/beads.db`) is the live store. `.beads/checkpoint/` is the
git-tracked durable checkpoint, and mutations do not flush it implicitly.

Flush explicitly before committing bead state:

```bash
bead sync flush-only
./scripts/checkpoint-publish.sh stage
```

The staging helper resolves and verifies the generation objects named by both
checkpoint pointers, stages those objects atomically with the pointers, and
removes superseded `objects/gen-*.jsonl` files from the working tree. Install
the tracked pre-commit check once per clone with
`./scripts/install-git-hooks.sh`. Do not use `git add -A` for checkpoint
publication.

`bead doctor` is read-only by default. If a database is missing, wrong-schema,
or corrupt, confirm the backend first and restore an empty native store from
the committed forensic checkpoint with the documented `bead init` plus `bead
sync import-only --restore-into-empty` procedure. Never delete or rebuild a
bead database without explicitly accounting for unflushed work.

## Commits

Use the bead identifier when the work is bead-driven:

```text
feat(needle-XYZ): short description
fix(needle-XYZ): short description
test(needle-XYZ): short description
```

Do not mix unrelated cleanup into the task commit. State which checks were run
and any remaining limitations in the final handoff or bead notes.

## Telemetry Contract

NEEDLE emits OpenTelemetry-compatible telemetry via OTLP. When modifying code that interacts with the telemetry system, maintain these semantic conventions:

### GenAI Attributes

The `agent.dispatch` span uses OpenTelemetry's `gen_ai.*` semantic conventions:

| Attribute | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `gen_ai.system` | AI provider (e.g., `anthropic`, `openai`) |
| `gen_ai.request.model` | Model identifier (e.g., `claude-sonnet-4-6`) |
| `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` | Input token count |
| `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens` | Output token count |

These attributes enable NEEDLE telemetry to integrate with GenAI-focused dashboards (Grafana GenAI app, Langfuse, Honeycomb AI, etc.).

### Resource Attributes

Every exported signal carries these resource attributes:

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| `service.name` | `"needle"` |
| `service.version` | Build version from `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` |
| `service.instance.id` | Worker ID (e.g., `needle-claude-anthropic-sonnet-alpha`) |
| `needle.session_id` | Per-boot random session ID |
| `host.name` | Hostname |
| `process.pid` | Worker PID |

For the complete semantic mapping of NEEDLE events to OpenTelemetry signals, see [`docs/plan/plan.md`](docs/plan/plan.md).

# Declarative Configuration Guide

This repository is the source of truth for cluster state. ArgoCD reconciles
every cluster from `main`, so a pushed manifest may deploy immediately.

## Before Editing

- Inspect `git status --short` and preserve all unrelated work. This repository
  is edited concurrently by agents on multiple machines.
- Read the closest nested `AGENTS.md`, especially the target cluster guide.
- Before starting, update with `git pull --rebase origin main` when doing so
  will not disturb another worker's uncommitted changes. Never merge or
  force-push.

## Changes and Delivery

- Make all desired-state changes in this repository. Do not directly mutate
  ArgoCD-managed cluster resources.
- Keep commits narrowly scoped. After each commit, push immediately to
  `origin main`; do not batch local commits.
- If a push is rejected, run `git pull --rebase origin main`, resolve carefully,
  and push again. Do not overwrite another contributor's work.
- Validate manifests before committing. After pushing, use read-only cluster or
  ArgoCD inspection to confirm the relevant Application is `Synced` and
  `Healthy`; a successful push alone is not completion.

## Secrets

- Never commit plaintext credentials or a populated `kind: Secret`. Use the
  repository's documented template and SealedSecret workflow.
- Before committing, ensure both `pre-commit` and `gitleaks` are installed and
  that `pre-commit install` has been run for this clone. Hooks are local and do
  not arrive with a clone.
- Do not bypass failed secret-scanning hooks. If sensitive data appears in any
  output or diff, stop and remove it without repeating the value.

Kubernetes layout, naming, resource, storage, ingress, ArgoCD, and validation
rules are in `k8s/AGENTS.md`.
--- k8s AGENTS ---
# Kubernetes Manifest Guide

These manifests are deployed by ArgoCD. Follow the repository-root guide and
the target cluster's `AGENTS.md` before editing.

## Layout and Discovery

- Use `k8s/<cluster>/<namespace>/`; every namespace directory must contain
  `namespace.yml`.
- Namespace directories are flat. Put every manifest directly in that directory
  and use `<app>-<kind>.yml` prefixes instead of subdirectories.
- Prefer `.yml` and stay consistent with neighboring files. Append `.disabled`
  to prevent discovery temporarily.
- ArgoCD `Application` manifests must end in `-application.yml` or
  `-application.yaml`. Namespace sync excludes these files; the app-of-apps
  layer discovers them. A different suffix silently prevents deployment.

## Capacity and Workloads

- Read the target cluster's `AGENTS.md` before adding or resizing a workload.
  Size against allocatable capacity and the largest single node, not advertised
  instance size or cluster totals. A pod must fit on one node.
- Run `./k8s/capacity-check.sh <cluster>` for current committed/free capacity;
  do not treat committed figures in documentation as live state.
- Always set realistic CPU and memory requests. Add requests when touching an
  existing BestEffort workload. On small clusters keep memory limits at most
  twice memory requests and never above one node's allocatable memory.
- `kind: Job` and `kind: CronJob` are banned. Use a Deployment whose application
  performs its own scheduling loop so ArgoCD retains ownership and pruning.
- Private images require the registry pull secret available in that namespace.
  Verify the secret name through read-only inspection rather than guessing.
- Pin every image. Never use `:latest`; `ronaldraygun/*` images must use a
  `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` tag, not a bare commit SHA. Container repositories keep
  the release version in `containers/<name>/VERSION` and manifests are updated
  after a successful build.

## Secrets

- Never commit a populated core `Secret`. Commit an app-specific
  `<app>-secret.yml.template` plus a SealedSecret.
- Each placeholder in the template needs an inline instruction explaining how
  to obtain or generate it. Do not use a generic `secret.yml.template` name.
- Fill a temporary Secret locally, seal it for the target cluster, and delete
  the plaintext file immediately. SealedSecrets are cluster-specific.
- A path such as `secret/<cluster>/...` is authoritative in that cluster's
  OpenBao. Copies elsewhere are backups. Before rotating or diagnosing, use
  read-only inspection of the consumer's `ClusterSecretStore` server and write
  only to the owning instance through the authorized secret-management flow.

## Networking

- Use Traefik `IngressRoute`, never Kubernetes `Ingress`.
- `websecure` is public through Cloudflare; `vpn` is mesh-only. Add only the
  entrypoints the service needs. Prefer the `vpn` entrypoint for HTTP(S) over
  creating another Tailscale proxy.
- Every IngressRoute, including VPN-only routes, needs a per-service Certificate
  and `tls.secretName`; bare `tls: {}` is invalid. Public routes normally use
  the shared auth middleware. VPN-only routes need no external-DNS annotation.
- Cloudflare hostnames must be one label below the domain; use a hyphen such as
  `api-staging.ardenone.com`, not `api.staging.ardenone.com`.
- Use `tailscale.com/expose` for non-HTTP services needing a tailnet hostname,
  and a selector-less Service with `tailscale.com/tailnet-fqdn` for cross-cluster
  egress.

## Storage

- On every Rackspace Spot cluster, set `storageClassName` explicitly to `sata`
  or `sata-large`. Never use `ssd`, `ssd-large`, `local-path`, or an implicit
  default there.
- Rackspace node pools are managed outside this repository. Use spot pools only;
  do not represent node-pool changes in these manifests.

## ArgoCD and Helm Applications

- Let Helm release naming derive from the Application name, conventionally
  `<chart>-<cluster>`. Never set `fullnameOverride` or `nameOverride`; doing so
  can duplicate resources and break webhook TLS names.
- Use Helm `parameters` for simple scalar chart settings and `valuesObject` for
  nested configuration. Pin chart `targetRevision`.
- Automated Applications should enable prune, self-heal, empty-result handling,
  validation, namespace creation, foreground/prune-last behavior, respect for
  ignored differences, server-side apply, bounded retry, and revision history.
  Follow a neighboring current Application rather than reconstructing the
  complete policy from memory.
- Tailscale-managed Services need ignored differences for operator-owned type,
  external name, finalizers, and status fields.
- Set an Application destination to the actual target cluster server. Use
  `https://kubernetes.default.svc` only for a self-managing in-cluster target.

## Validation and Observation

- Compare with neighboring manifests, render Helm/Kustomize where applicable,
  and run available schema or repository checks before committing.
- Cluster access for routine verification is read-only. Do not use `kubectl`
  apply/create/delete/patch/edit/annotate/scale/rollout. A targeted ArgoCD sync
  may apply already-committed desired state only when a narrower guide or the
  task's authorized delivery procedure explicitly calls for it.
- After push, inspect the owning ArgoCD Application and relevant pods/events/logs
  until it is `Synced` and `Healthy`. Check for CRD validation failures, webhook
  TLS/name conflicts, duplicate ownership, pull failures, Pending pods, and
  deployment progress deadlines.
- Argo Workflows run in `iad-ci`; templates live under
  `k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/`. Completed pods may be removed immediately by
  `podGC`, so stream logs while running or use the retained Argo UI logs.

## Final Review Checklist

- Flat namespace directory with `namespace.yml`.
- No plaintext Secret, Job, CronJob, standard Ingress, or `:latest` image.
- Requests fit the target cluster and one node; private pulls name a real secret.
- Spot PVCs use `sata`/`sata-large`; ingress has the right visibility and TLS.
- Application filename, Helm naming, destination, and pinned revisions are
  correct; pre-push checks pass and post-push reconciliation is healthy.
--- iad-ci AGENTS ---
# iad-ci Agent Guide

This directory defines the burst-oriented CI/CD cluster managed by rs-manager
ArgoCD. Make desired-state changes here; do not mutate ArgoCD-managed live
resources. Read `CLAUDE.md` for additional operational context.

## Capacity and placement

- Stable node shapes are three `compute1-8` nodes (3.50 CPU / 6.16 GiB
  allocatable each) and three `compute1-4` nodes (1.50 CPU / 2.54 GiB each),
  for a point-in-time total of 15 CPU / 26.08 GiB allocatable.
- The autoscaler changes node count and names. Use
  `./k8s/capacity-check.sh iad-ci`; do not rely on recorded utilization.
- Default workflow-step requests are `250m` CPU / `512Mi`; long-lived services
  default to `50m` / `128Mi` and should normally live on another cluster.
- Keep steps at or below 1.5 CPU / 2.5 GiB to fit every node. Larger steps can
  use only `compute1-8`; nothing above 3.50 CPU / 6.16 GiB can schedule.
- Keep memory limits at most 2x requests and at most 6 GiB.

## Workflow and storage rules

- Set requests on every container and pin every image version or digest; never
  use `:latest`.
- Preserve workflow cleanup (`podGC`) and ensure per-run PVCs are removed. The
  nightly fuzz workflow has historically leaked unbound claims; fix leaks in
  `argo-workflows/`, not by live deletion.
- Every PVC and `volumeClaimTemplate` must explicitly use `sata` or
  `sata-large`. The default `ssd` class is prohibited. Cinder volumes cannot be
  expanded.
- Completed pods disappear under `podGC: OnPodCompletion`; stream logs while a
  failing step runs or use a deliberate debug workflow with
  `OnWorkflowCompletion`.

## Before merging

Run `./k8s/check-resource-limits.py iad-ci` and fix anything it reports as
critical before merging -- it checks every WorkflowTemplate/CronWorkflow/
Sensor manifest against the ceilings above and the storage/image rules below.
It answers "can this ever schedule," not "is there room right now" -- also run
`./k8s/capacity-check.sh iad-ci` to confirm burst-build headroom against
current load. Cluster inspection is read-only; see `CLAUDE.md` for the current
kubeconfig and UI access.

/home/coding/declarative-config/docs/sensor-wedge-analysis-report.md-332-The lack of recent workflow triggers for most sensors is due to **low event volume**, NOT a wedge. When events arrive, sensors process them correctly.
/home/coding/declarative-config/docs/sensor-wedge-analysis-report.md-333-

/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md-48-| Component | Responsibility | Inputs | Outputs |
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md-49-|-----------|---------------|--------|---------|
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md-50-| **CLI** | Parse commands, manage sessions | User commands | Worker processes |
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md:51:| **Worker** | Execute the strand waterfall loop | Bead queue state | Dispatch requests, state transitions |
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md-52-| **StrandRunner** | Evaluate strands in sequence | Queue state, config | Next bead or escalation |
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md-53-| **Claimer** | Atomic bead claiming with serialization | Candidate bead ID | Claimed bead or race-lost signal |
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md-54-| **PromptBuilder** | Construct deterministic prompts from bead context | Claimed bead | Prompt string |
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md-55-| **Dispatcher** | Load adapter, render template, execute agent | Prompt, adapter config | Agent process handle |
--
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md-111-| Bundler shipped undefined functions | Compiled language eliminates this class entirely. |
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md-112-| Agent-owned closure most reliable | NEEDLE does not close beads. Agent receives `br close <id>` instruction in prompt. |
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md-113-| stdout/stderr corruption | Telemetry is a structured system, never interleaved with agent output. |
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md-114-| Workers modifying their own orchestrator | Self-modification allowed via release channels. New builds must pass canary tests in isolation before promotion to `:stable`. Fleet hot-reloads from `:stable`, never from `:testing`. |
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md:115:| ~20 worker practical limit (EX44) | Fleet sizing is bounded by three runtime factors: provider inference throughput, available CPU, and available RAM. NEEDLE monitors these and warns when saturated. Staggered launch is default. |
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md-116-| Bead granularity affects success rate | Document guidelines but don't enforce — this is a bead authoring concern, not orchestration. |

/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md-1755-
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md:1756:### Fleet Sizing
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md-1757-
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md-1758-The practical worker limit is not an arbitrary number. It is driven by three runtime constraints:
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md-1759-
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md:1760:1. **Provider inference throughput.** Each worker waiting on an LLM response is idle CPU but an active API slot. If the provider rate-limits or queues requests, adding workers produces no additional throughput. NEEDLE tracks RPM per provider and warns when request latency exceeds a threshold.
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md-1761-
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md-1762-2. **Available CPU.** Each agent process (Claude Code, OpenCode, etc.) consumes CPU during tool execution, file I/O, and git operations. NEEDLE's own overhead (strand evaluation, heartbeat I/O, lock contention) also scales with worker count. When system load exceeds a configurable threshold, NEEDLE emits a `fleet.cpu_saturated` warning.
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md-1763-
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md-1764-3. **Available RAM.** Each agent process holds context in memory. Agent processes with large context windows or many tool calls can consume significant RAM. NEEDLE monitors system memory and warns when free memory drops below a threshold.
--
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md-1771-  cpu_load_warn: 0.8          # warn when system load average > 80% of cores
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md-1772-  memory_free_warn_mb: 512    # warn when free memory < 512MB
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md-1773-```
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md-1774-
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md:1775:If `max_workers` is set, it is enforced at launch time. `needle run --count=25` with `max_workers: 20` will launch 20 and log a warning. If set to 0, NEEDLE launches the requested count and relies on runtime monitoring to signal saturation.
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md-1776-

/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md-2045-| `worker.session` | `needle.beads_processed`, `needle.uptime_seconds`, `needle.exit_reason` |

/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md:2049:| `agent.dispatch` | `gen_ai.system` (e.g., `anthropic`), `gen_ai.request.model`, `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`, `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens`, `needle.agent.pid`, `needle.agent.exit_code` |
/home/coding/NEEDLE/docs/plan/plan.md-2050-| `bead.outcome` | `needle.outcome` (`success` / `failure` / `timeout` / `crash` / `agent_not_found` / `interrupted`), `needle.outcome.action` |

--- bead help ---
bead-rs is an independent Rust task-coordination system.

The intended workflow is:
  init workspace -> create beads -> add blocking relationships
  -> inspect ready work -> claim -> update/release -> close -> flush checkpoint

The ready frontier can be inspected with `bead list --ready --json --limit N`,
which uses claim order but does not reserve the displayed beads. Use `bead claim`
to atomically assign work.

SQLite (.beads/beads.db) is the authoritative live state between flushes, and is
not committed. The checkpoint under .beads/checkpoint/ is the portable, durable
copy and is what Git tracks; flush it with `bead sync flush-only` before
committing the repository. Mutating commands never flush implicitly.

Lifecycle transitions:
  - open beads may be ready if unassigned and not manually blocked
  - unfinished `blocks` edges remove beads from the ready frontier
  - claim atomically assigns one ready bead and moves it to in_progress
  - release returns claimed work to open/unassigned
  - close requires a reason and may expose dependents
  - reopen restores a closed bead to open

EXIT CODES:
  0  success
  1  internal failure
  2  CLI usage or validation error
  3  workspace, issue, or file not found
  4  conflict (invalid transition, revision guard, cycle)
  5  malformed input or integrity failure

Run `bead <COMMAND> --help` for the full description of any command.

Usage: bead <COMMAND>

Commands:
  init          Initialize a new workspace
  create        Create a new issue
  list          List issues
  show          Show a single issue
  update        Update an issue
  release       Release a claimed issue
  close         Close an issue
  reopen        Reopen a closed issue
  claim         Claim an issue from the ready frontier
  label         Manage labels
  dep           Manage dependencies
  ref           Manage external references
  sync          Synchronize checkpoint operations
  doctor        Diagnose workspace integrity and optionally perform repairs
  capabilities  Show capabilities and supported features
  schema        Inspect public schemas
  query         Execute safe query language queries
  changes       Access cursor-based change feed for incremental local synchronization
  why           Explain issue state, readiness, blockers, and legal operations
  compare       Compare issue representation across two profiles
  data          Manage structured bead data
  recurrence    Manage recurrence templates
  policy        Validate workspace policy and scheduling configuration
  help          Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version
--- show help ---
Display detailed information about a single issue.

Shows complete issue details including dependencies, labels, and optionally
comments. Output format depends on --json flag.

EXAMPLES:
  bead show bead-123abc456789def                    # Human-readable output
  bead show ID --json                                # JSON output for NEEDLE
  bead show ID --comments unresolved                 # With unresolved comments
  bead show ID --comments all --json                 # Full issue with all comments

OUTPUT FORMAT:
  Without --json: Human-readable detailed view
  With --json: One-element JSON array for NEEDLE v1 compatibility

COMMENT PROJECTION:
  --comments none         Show only counts and resolution metadata (default)

  JSON output format is a one-element array containing the issue object.

ISSUE DETAILS INCLUDE:

  - Labels: all assigned labels
  - Comments: based on --comments projection
  - Metadata: issue_type, manual_blocked flag, close_reason (if closed)

.beads/checkpoint/objects/gen-40e94b5b41861e8139afbc8b9e4fb5d0.jsonl:286:{"issue":{"assignee":"claude-code","base_status":"closed","close_reason":"Fixed by 81b0995 (bf-z3yp0): Supervisor::tick() now sweeps waitpid(-1, WNOHANG) at the top of every tick, reaping exited worker children so they no longer accumulate as <defunct> zombies. GH #12.","closed_at":"2026-08-14T16:10:59.226590061Z","comments":[],"created_at":"2026-08-14T16:10:45.87365349Z","data":{},"dependencies":[{"blocker":"needle-70008678","kind":"blocks"}],"description":"Reported 2026-07-28 by jarvis-laboratories (same production adopter as GH #7-#11 / ADR-009), same ~900-bead monorepo cutover. GitHub issue: https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/issues/12. Full rationale: ADR-010 (docs/adr/010-supervisor-zombie-reaping.md), plan.md Phase 14.1.\n\nConfirmed against source: Supervisor::spawn_worker (src/supervisor/mod.rs:377-498) builds a detached child (setsid via pre_exec, process_group(0), null stdio) and calls cmd.spawn()? (line 488) with the returned std::process::Child immediately dropped — never bound to a variable, so there is no way to later .wait()/.try_wait() on it. setsid/process_group detach the child from the controlling terminal/session only; they do NOT detach it from being a reapable child of the supervisor process. A crate-wide grep for waitpid|try_wait|SIGCHLD|\\.wait() finds reaping logic only in src/dispatch/mod.rs, src/telemetry/mod.rs, src/canary/mod.rs — all different child processes (agent dispatch, telemetry subprocess, canary binary checks), none of them supervisor-spawned workers. Rust's Child::drop does not reap a process.\n\nProduction evidence (reporter's cutover soak, pin v0.2.12/fad0b50): 22 [needle ...] <defunct> zombies under needle-supervise after ~15 minutes of operation.\n\nSuggested fix (already validated as a local patch in the reporter's production fork, and the decision in ADR-010): add a reap sweep at the top of Supervisor::tick() (src/supervisor/mod.rs) — loop libc::waitpid(-1, &mut status, libc::WNOHANG) until it returns 0 (nothing left to reap right now) or -1 with errno == ECHILD (no children at all). Safe because needle supervise only ever directly spawns worker processes; gate commands/dispatch subprocesses run inside the worker process (a separate PID tree), so this cannot race with the .wait() calls already present elsewhere for different child processes.\n\nAlternatives considered and rejected in ADR-010: double-fork + reparent to init (bigger change than needed); retaining Child handles + try_wait per tick (would require new Supervisor state for no benefit over the sweep, since nothing else needs live child handles).\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n- Supervisor::tick() reaps any exited worker child within one poll_interval_secs tick — no zombie process-table entries accumulate for the lifetime of a long-running needle supervise daemon.\n- Regression test: spawn a real short-lived child (e.g. true), let it exit, assert it is a zombie before the sweep runs, assert the sweep reaps it.\n- No change to spawn_worker's detach model (setsid + process_group(0)) — this is a missing-reap fix, not a re-architecture.\n- cargo test --lib passes; no clippy warnings; needle-ci green on push.","external_references":[],"id":"needle-43b3a763","issue_type":"bug","manual_blocked":false,"notes":"","priority":1,"profile":"native-v1","revision":2,"schema_ref":"urn:bead-rs:schema:issue:native-v1","title":"Supervisor never reaps spawned workers — zombies accumulate under needle supervise (GH #12)","updated_at":"2026-08-14T16:10:59.226590061Z"},"record_type":"issue"}

--- live capacity script ---
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Regenerate the capacity numbers quoted in each k8s/<cluster>/CLAUDE.md.
#
#   ./k8s/capacity-check.sh              # all clusters
#   ./k8s/capacity-check.sh iad-ci       # one cluster
#
# Reports, per cluster: node shapes, allocatable vs committed requests,
# per-node free space, and the largest single pod that can still schedule.
# The last number is the one that matters — a pod bigger than the largest
# per-node gap stays Pending forever no matter how much cluster-wide free
# capacity the totals suggest.
set -uo pipefail

declare -A ACCESS=(
  [apexalgo-iad]="--server=http://traefik-apexalgo-iad:8001"
  [ardenone-cluster]="--server=http://traefik-ardenone-cluster:8001"
  [ardenone-manager]="--server=http://traefik-ardenone-manager:8001"
  [rs-manager]="--server=http://traefik-rs-manager:8001"
  [iad-ci]="--kubeconfig=/home/coding/.kube/iad-ci.kubeconfig"
  [iad-kalshi]="--server=http://kubectl-proxy-iad-kalshi:8001"
  [iad-options]="--server=http://traefik-iad-options:8001"
  [ord-devimprint]="--server=http://kubectl-proxy-ord-devimprint:8001"
)

CLUSTERS=("${@:-}")
[ -z "${CLUSTERS[0]:-}" ] && CLUSTERS=("${!ACCESS[@]}")

for c in "${CLUSTERS[@]}"; do
  flags="${ACCESS[$c]:-}"
  if [ -z "$flags" ]; then echo "unknown cluster: $c" >&2; continue; fi
  tmp=$(mktemp -d)
  trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
  if ! timeout 60 kubectl $flags get nodes -o json > "$tmp/nodes.json" 2>/dev/null ||
     ! timeout 120 kubectl $flags get pods -A -o json > "$tmp/pods.json" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "### $c — UNREACHABLE"; echo; rm -rf "$tmp"; continue
  fi
  CLUSTER="$c" DATA="$tmp" python3 - <<'PY'
import json, os, collections

def cpu(v):
    if not v: return 0.0
    v = str(v)
    return float(v[:-1])/1000 if v.endswith('m') else float(v)

def mem(v):
    if not v: return 0.0
    v = str(v)
    units = {'Ki':1024, 'Mi':1024**2, 'Gi':1024**3, 'Ti':1024**4, 'K':1e3, 'M':1e6, 'G':1e9}
    for suffix, mult in sorted(units.items(), key=lambda x: -len(x[0])):
        if v.endswith(suffix): return float(v[:-len(suffix)]) * mult
    return float(v)

G = 1024**3
c = os.environ['CLUSTER']
data = os.environ['DATA']
nodes = json.load(open(f"{data}/nodes.json"))['items']
pods = json.load(open(f"{data}/pods.json"))['items']

alloc, shapes = {}, collections.Counter()
for n in nodes:
    a = n['status']['allocatable']
    cap = n['status']['capacity']
    alloc[n['metadata']['name']] = (cpu(a['cpu']), mem(a['memory']))
    it = n['metadata'].get('labels', {}).get('node.kubernetes.io/instance-type', '?')
    shapes[f"{it} ({cpu(cap['cpu']):.0f}c/{mem(cap['memory'])/G:.1f}Gi cap -> "
           f"{cpu(a['cpu']):.2f}c/{mem(a['memory'])/G:.2f}Gi alloc)"] += 1

used = collections.defaultdict(lambda: [0.0, 0.0, 0])
unscheduled = [0.0, 0.0, 0]
for p in pods:
    if p['status'].get('phase') in ('Succeeded', 'Failed'): continue
    rc = sum(cpu((ct.get('resources', {}).get('requests') or {}).get('cpu'))
             for ct in p['spec']['containers'])
    rm = sum(mem((ct.get('resources', {}).get('requests') or {}).get('memory'))
             for ct in p['spec']['containers'])
    node = p['spec'].get('nodeName')
    if node:
        e = used[node]; e[0] += rc; e[1] += rm; e[2] += 1
    else:
        unscheduled[0] += rc; unscheduled[1] += rm; unscheduled[2] += 1

print(f"### {c} — {len(nodes)} nodes")
for shape, count in shapes.items():
    print(f"    {count}x {shape}")
free_c, free_m = [], []
for name, (ac, am) in sorted(alloc.items()):
    uc, um, n_pods = used[name]
    fc, fm = ac - uc, am - um
    free_c.append(fc); free_m.append(fm)
    print(f"    {name[:38]:38} {uc:5.2f}/{ac:.2f}c ({100*uc/ac:3.0f}%)  "
          f"{um/G:6.2f}/{am/G:5.2f}Gi ({100*um/am:3.0f}%)  pods={n_pods:3}  "
          f"free {fc:5.2f}c/{fm/G:5.2f}Gi")
tot_c = sum(v[0] for v in alloc.values())
tot_m = sum(v[1] for v in alloc.values())
print(f"    TOTAL allocatable : {tot_c:.2f} CPU / {tot_m/G:.2f} GiB")
print(f"    TOTAL committed   : {tot_c-sum(free_c):.2f} CPU "
      f"({100*(tot_c-sum(free_c))/tot_c:.0f}%) / {(tot_m-sum(free_m))/G:.2f} GiB "
      f"({100*(tot_m-sum(free_m))/tot_m:.0f}%)")
print(f"    LARGEST POD THAT FITS: {max(free_c):.2f} CPU / {max(free_m)/G:.2f} GiB")
if unscheduled[2]:
    print(f"    !! UNSCHEDULED: {unscheduled[2]} pods wanting "
          f"{unscheduled[0]:.2f}c/{unscheduled[1]/G:.2f}Gi")
print()
PY
  rm -rf "$tmp"
done
--- resource checker ---
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check every WorkflowTemplate/CronWorkflow/Sensor manifest in a k8s/<cluster>
directory against that cluster's hard scheduling ceiling and the repo's
sizing/storage conventions (see CLAUDE.md's "Cluster Sizing" section and
k8s/<cluster>/CLAUDE.md's own per-node table).

This complements capacity-check.sh, not replaces it: capacity-check.sh
reports live, current headroom on a running cluster; this reads committed
manifest source and answers a different question -- "can this pod, as
written, EVER schedule on this cluster's biggest node," independent of
current load. A manifest can pass this check and still queue behind other
work; a manifest that fails this check will never run no matter how idle
the cluster is.

Usage:
  k8s/check-resource-limits.py <cluster> [--cpu-ceiling-m N] [--mem-ceiling-mi N]

Exit 0 if clean, 1 if any critical (never-schedulable) finding exists.
Low-severity (memory limit >2x request) findings are reported but do not
fail the check -- they're a looseness warning, not a scheduling blocker.

Born from a 2026-08-12 audit of iad-ci: 78 of 147 WorkflowTemplates carried
the same copy-pasted 4000m/8Gi (sometimes 8000m/16Gi) limit block, which
can never schedule on any node in that cluster (biggest node: 3.50 CPU /
6.16Gi allocatable). All fixed same day; this script exists so the next
copy-paste gets caught before merge instead of silently failing forever.
"""
import argparse
import glob
import re
import sys

import yaml

CPU_RE = re.compile(r"^(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)(m)?$")
MEM_RE = re.compile(r"^(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)(Ei|Pi|Ti|Gi|Mi|Ki|E|P|T|G|M|K)?$")
MEM_MULT_MI = {
    "Ki": 1 / 1024, "Mi": 1, "Gi": 1024, "Ti": 1024 * 1024,
    "K": 1000 / 1024, "M": 1000 * 1000 / (1024 * 1024),
    "G": 1000 * 1000 * 1000 / (1024 * 1024), "T": 1000 ** 4 / (1024 * 1024),
    None: 1 / (1024 * 1024),
}


def parse_cpu_m(v):
    if v is None:
        return None
    m = CPU_RE.match(str(v))
    if not m:
        return None
    num = float(m.group(1))
    return num if m.group(2) == "m" else num * 1000


def parse_mem_mi(v):
    if v is None:
        return None
    m = MEM_RE.match(str(v))
    if not m:
        return None
    mult = MEM_MULT_MI.get(m.group(2))
    return float(m.group(1)) * mult if mult is not None else None


def walk(node, path, findings, ctx, cpu_ceiling, mem_ceiling):
    if isinstance(node, dict):
        if isinstance(node.get("resources"), dict):
            check_resources(node, path, findings, ctx, cpu_ceiling, mem_ceiling)
        img = node.get("image")
        if isinstance(img, str) and img.startswith("ronaldraygun/") and img.endswith(":latest"):
            findings.append((ctx, path, "critical", f"ronaldraygun image uses :latest -- {img}"))
        for k, v in node.items():
            if k == "volumeClaimTemplates" and isinstance(v, list):
                for i, vct in enumerate(v):
                    check_pvc(vct, f"{path}.volumeClaimTemplates[{i}]", findings, ctx)
            else:
                walk(v, f"{path}.{k}" if path else k, findings, ctx, cpu_ceiling, mem_ceiling)
    elif isinstance(node, list):
        for i, item in enumerate(node):
            walk(item, f"{path}[{i}]", findings, ctx, cpu_ceiling, mem_ceiling)


def check_resources(container_like, path, findings, ctx, cpu_ceiling, mem_ceiling):
    res = container_like.get("resources") or {}
    requests = res.get("requests") or {}
    limits = res.get("limits") or {}
    cname = container_like.get("name", "?")

    if not requests.get("cpu") or not requests.get("memory"):
        findings.append((ctx, path, "medium", f"'{cname}' missing resources.requests"))

    cpu_lim = parse_cpu_m(limits.get("cpu"))
    if cpu_lim is not None and cpu_lim > cpu_ceiling:
        findings.append((ctx, path, "critical",
            f"'{cname}' cpu limit {limits.get('cpu')} exceeds {cpu_ceiling:.0f}m ceiling -- can never schedule"))

    mem_lim = parse_mem_mi(limits.get("memory"))
    if mem_lim is not None and mem_lim > mem_ceiling:
        findings.append((ctx, path, "critical",
            f"'{cname}' memory limit {limits.get('memory')} exceeds {mem_ceiling:.0f}Mi ceiling -- can never schedule"))

    mem_req = parse_mem_mi(requests.get("memory"))
    if mem_lim is not None and mem_req:
        ratio = mem_lim / mem_req
        if ratio > 2.01:
            findings.append((ctx, path, "low",
                f"'{cname}' memory limit is {ratio:.1f}x request ({requests.get('memory')} -> {limits.get('memory')})"))


def check_pvc(vct, path, findings, ctx):
    sc = (vct.get("spec") or {}).get("storageClassName")
    if not sc:
        findings.append((ctx, path, "critical", "volumeClaimTemplate has no storageClassName (inherits banned default)"))
    elif sc not in ("sata", "sata-large"):
        findings.append((ctx, path, "critical", f"volumeClaimTemplate storageClassName={sc!r}, must be sata/sata-large"))


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("cluster")
    ap.add_argument("--cpu-ceiling-m", type=float, default=3500)
    ap.add_argument("--mem-ceiling-mi", type=float, default=6144)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    base = f"k8s/{args.cluster}"
    files = sorted(
        glob.glob(f"{base}/argo-workflows/*.yml") + glob.glob(f"{base}/argo-workflows/*.yaml")
        + glob.glob(f"{base}/argo-events/*.yml") + glob.glob(f"{base}/argo-events/*.yaml")
    )
    if not files:
        print(f"no argo-workflows/argo-events manifests found under {base}/", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    findings = []
    for fpath in files:
        with open(fpath) as f:
            try:
                docs = list(yaml.safe_load_all(f))
            except yaml.YAMLError as e:
                findings.append((("?", "?", fpath), "", "low", f"YAML parse error (not necessarily a real bug -- verify manually): {e}"))
                continue
        for doc in docs:
            if not isinstance(doc, dict):
                continue
            kind = doc.get("kind", "")
            if kind not in ("WorkflowTemplate", "ClusterWorkflowTemplate", "CronWorkflow", "Workflow", "Sensor"):
                continue
            name = doc.get("metadata", {}).get("name", "?")
            ctx = (kind, name, fpath)
            walk(doc.get("spec", {}), "spec", findings, ctx, args.cpu_ceiling_m, args.mem_ceiling_mi)

    order = {"critical": 0, "medium": 1, "low": 2}
    findings.sort(key=lambda f: (order.get(f[2], 9), f[0][2]))

    n_crit = sum(1 for f in findings if f[2] == "critical")
    for ctx, path, sev, msg in findings:
        kind, name, fpath = ctx
        print(f"[{sev.upper()}] {fpath} ({kind}/{name}) {path}: {msg}")

    print(f"\n{len(files)} files checked, {len(findings)} findings, {n_crit} critical")
    sys.exit(1 if n_crit else 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

bead-rs is an independent Rust task-coordination system.

The intended workflow is:
  init workspace -> create beads -> add blocking relationships
  -> inspect ready work -> claim -> update/release -> close -> flush checkpoint

The ready frontier can be inspected with `bead list --ready --json --limit N`,
which uses claim order but does not reserve the displayed beads. Use `bead claim`
to atomically assign work.

SQLite (.beads/beads.db) is the authoritative live state between flushes, and is
not committed. The checkpoint under .beads/checkpoint/ is the portable, durable
copy and is what Git tracks; flush it with `bead sync flush-only` before
committing the repository. Mutating commands never flush implicitly.

Lifecycle transitions:
  - open beads may be ready if unassigned and not manually blocked
  - unfinished `blocks` edges remove beads from the ready frontier
  - claim atomically assigns one ready bead and moves it to in_progress
  - release returns claimed work to open/unassigned
  - close requires a reason and may expose dependents
  - reopen restores a closed bead to open

EXIT CODES:
  0  success
  1  internal failure
  2  CLI usage or validation error
  3  workspace, issue, or file not found
  4  conflict (invalid transition, revision guard, cycle)
  5  malformed input or integrity failure

    servers.ngpc.rxt.io/class=ch.vs1.large-iad, restricting all CI to the three
    compute1-8 nodes and walling off the three compute1-4 nodes (4.50 CPU /
    7.62 GiB allocatable) entirely. Measured today: large nodes at 71/80/97%
    committed CPU while a small node sat at 13%, cluster-wide only 72%.
    
    needle-ci-8x2jj hit the consequence — Pending for its full 2h
    activeDeadlineSeconds, never ran a test, reported as a deadline breach with no
    logs. Five concurrent kaniko pods from one ACB build (1 CPU / 2Gi each) held all
    three eligible nodes.
    
    Two changes:
    
    1. Remove the default nodeSelector. requests already determine where a pod can
       fit; a step needing >1.50 CPU / 2.54 GiB lands on a compute1-8 because no
       compute1-4 can satisfy it. Class-pinning on top only removes options. Steps
       that truly need a large node should declare their own selector.
    
    2. needle-ci CPU request 2000m -> 1500m, to comply with the cap in
       k8s/iad-ci/CLAUDE.md ('workflow step requests <= 1.5 CPU so any node can take
       it'), which this template was violating. Memory request stays 4Gi on purpose:
       cargo build --release with lto=true is the memory peak, and under-requesting
       it trades a scheduling stall for an OOM mid-link.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

{"assignee":null,"comments":[],"created_at":"2026-08-14T16:10:52.179887028Z","dependencies":[],"description":"Compounding half of GH #12 (https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/issues/12), same report as bf-12bim (reap sweep). Full rationale: ADR-010 (docs/adr/010-supervisor-zombie-reaping.md), plan.md Phase 14.2.\n\nConfirmed against source: registry::is_pid_alive (src/registry/mod.rs:28-52) checks liveness via kill(pid, 0) == 0 (with errno ESRCH/EPERM disambiguation). kill(pid, 0) succeeds for a zombie (state Z) exactly as it does for a genuinely running process — a zombie still holds a PID table entry, it just hasn't been reaped yet (see bf-12bim). This is not a hypothetical concern: Supervisor::tick() (src/supervisor/mod.rs:308-336) filters registered workers with is_pid_alive(w.pid) (line 316) to compute alive_count, then gates new spawns on alive_count >= self.config.max_workers (line 335). So every unreaped worker zombie is counted as alive by the supervisor's own tick, artificially inflating alive_count and potentially blocking new worker spawns at exactly the moment real capacity exists. The reporter's issue explicitly connects this to a 'false max_workers capacity and silent hung supervise logs' observation during their cutover soak (compounded on their host by an unrelated large zombie population from PID 1 not reaping its own children).\n\nstrand::mend's liveness check (src/strand/mend.rs:707) also calls registry::is_pid_alive and inherits this same bug.\n\nSuggested fix (decision in ADR-010): on Linux, additionally check /proc/<pid>/stat's process-state field (the character after the second ')' in the comm field, robust to command names containing parentheses) and treat state Z as NOT alive, even though kill(pid, 0) still succeeds for it. {"assignee":null,"comments":[],"created_at":"2026-08-14T16:10:48.744362704Z","dependencies":[],"description":"Discovered 2026-07-28 while adding tests for bf-3pc1r/bf-j8o7w (GH #8/#9, commit e97e88a). CommandGate::run_command (src/validation/mod.rs) calls the fully synchronous, blocking std::process::Command::output() with no .await point during a gate command's execution. tokio::time::timeout's Timeout::poll polls the wrapped future first and only checks its deadline if that poll returns Pending -- so a wrapped future with no yield point during a slow blocking segment always completes before the deadline check can matter.\n\nNet effect: validation.outcome_timeout_seconds (now configurable per GH #8) can only observe, after the fact, that a gate command ran longer than the configured timeout -- it cannot actually cut the command off mid-execution the way its role (outcome-handler gate timeout) implies. A gate command that hangs or runs very long will block the whole outcome-handling task for its full duration regardless of the configured timeout value.\n\nFirst discovered via a broken test: an initial version of a handle_with_cancellation test used a slow verification: gate command (sleep 2) to try to trigger a 1s configured timeout, and it failed on iad-ci (workflow needle-ci-g7cqh) because the gate ran to completion (2s) before the timeout could ever be observed. The test was corrected (commit 4d8820f) to use a genuinely-async slow store operation instead, which does correctly demonstrate the config value is honored for the *other* (already-async) operations handle() performs -- just not for gate command execution itself.\n\nSuggested fix: run CommandGate's std::process::Command::output() inside tokio::task::spawn_blocking, so the returned JoinHandle future is a genuine yield point tokio::time::timeout can race against. The underlying OS process would still need its own kill-on-timeout handling (spawn_blocking alone doesn't kill the child process if the JoinHandle is abandoned) to avoid leaking a runaway subprocess after the outer timeout fires -- worth designing deliberately rather than bolting on.\n\nAcceptance criteria: a gate command configured to run longer than validation.outcome_timeout_seconds is actually interrupted (its OS process killed, not just outlived) at approximately the configured timeout, with a regression test proving it (a slow gate command + short configured timeout observed to return around the timeout, not after the full command duration).","id":"needle-6c89e8d3","labels":[],"priority":2,"revision":2,"status":"closed","title":"outcome_timeout_seconds cannot preempt a slow gate command (blocking subprocess, no async yield point)","updated_at":"2026-08-14T16:11:00.771064279Z"}

ID: needle-0339c178
Title: needle-ci pod cannot schedule: 2000m/4Gi request + large-node selector loses to concurrent kaniko builds
Status: Open
Priority: P1
Revision: 3
Created: 2026-08-14T16:10:51.118483808Z
Updated: 2026-08-15T18:34:51.178377527Z
Description: Observed live 2026-08-06 on needle-ci-8x2jj. The pod sat Pending for 78 minutes
and never started -- zero compilation, zero tests -- and is on track to be killed
by activeDeadlineSeconds (7200) at 13:18:25Z having done nothing at all.

Scheduler verdict (47 retries over 78 min):

  0/6 nodes are available: 3 Insufficient cpu, 3 Insufficient memory,
  3 node(s) did not match Pod node affinity/selector.

Why:
  - The pod carries nodeSelector servers.ngpc.rxt.io/class=ch.vs1.large-iad,
    which excludes the three compute1-4 nodes (1500m / 2.6Gi) outright. Only the
    three compute1-8 nodes (3500m / 6.16Gi) are ever eligible.
  - Those three are not empty. They also host forgejo, eventbus-default-js,
    calico, armor and victorialogs. Free CPU at the time of writing was 900m,
    900m and 1100m; free memory 1820Mi, 988Mi and 1948Mi.
  - needle-ci requests 2000m CPU and 4Gi. It fits on none of them.
  - The dominant occupier was a single ACB build: acb-bots-build-5kv8k ran FIVE
    concurrent kaniko pods at 1000m/2048Mi each (5 CPU, 10Gi total), spread
    1/2/2 across exactly those three nodes, for 99+ minutes.

So one unrelated multi-container build can monopolise every node needle-ci is
allowed to run on, and needle-ci then burns its entire 2h deadline in Pending.
This is a scheduling failure, not a slow build, and it is invisible in the
"Failed" status -- the workflow reports a deadline breach with no logs.

The template comment says the 2000m/4Gi request was deliberately sized against
the biggest node. That reasoning accounted for node capacity but not for the
resident system pods or for concurrent workflows.

Options, in declarative-config k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/needle-workflowtemplate.yml:
  - lower the CPU request so the pod fits alongside normal residents (the limit
    can stay high -- requests gate scheduling, limits gate throttling)

  --comments none         Show only counts and resolution metadata (default)
  --comments unresolved   Include bodies for unresolved comments only
  --comments all          Include all comment bodies in canonical order

NEEDLE COMPATIBILITY:
  JSON output format is a one-element array containing the issue object.
  This matches NEEDLE v1 expectations for subprocess output.

ISSUE DETAILS INCLUDE:
  - Basic fields: id, title, description, priority, status
  - Assignment: assignee (if any)
  - Timestamps: created_at, updated_at, closed_at (if closed)
  - Dependencies: blocked_by (blocking issues), blocking (issues this blocks)
  - Labels: all assigned labels
  - Comments: based on --comments projection
  - Metadata: issue_type, manual_blocked flag, close_reason (if closed)
